methods.description: Set out the source’s four-stage sum proof: verify the first permitted integer, write the full sum assumed at k, state the k+1 target with the next term and shifted right side, use the assumption in the algebra, then conclude for all integers from the verified start. Recognising a stage or supplying one requested component uses this same proof structure, not a separate method per label.

Use the same four-stage proof for divisibility, expressing the assumed k case as divisor times an integer and the next case as divisor times another integer. Verify the actual starting domain, and use the assumption to factor the next expression into the divisor and an integer. This integer-multiple working is distinct from matching a sum equality.

Check what the induction argument establishes: the step is conditional, a verified starting case is required, and the next-case link only carries truth upwards. A false first case disproves a universal claim even when the step is valid; a later verified case establishes only that case and those above it. Compare conclusions according to the question, including the strongest justified range.
